---
title: "Championships: NBA and WNBA eras"
---

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Why the time windows differ
- **NBA section:** **2005-06 to 2025-26**, starting with the first season that has salaries reported for about 99% of minutes.
- **WNBA section:** every WNBA season we have, **2009 to 2026**. WNBA salary records start only in 2021, and starting
  there would leave six champions to learn from.
- **NBA vs WNBA:** the two leagues are compared season against season, never pooled.
- **Models that learn from champions use all of each league's seasons in its window.** There is one champion per
  season, so a short window leaves too few champions to test a model.
- **Shot zones are calibrated by season.** ESPN's recorded shot positions drift between eras, most visibly in the
  WNBA's 2020 bubble season, so the rim zone is anchored to where layups are recorded each season (Data page).
:::

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from _viz import read, md, show, LEAGUE

START = {"NBA": 2006, "WNBA": 2009}
ZONES = ["three", "rim", "paint / short mid", "long mid"]
z = read("step5_playoff_zone_by_season.csv")
z = z[z.season >= z.league.map(START)]
ci = read("step5_champion_identity.csv")
ci = ci[ci.season >= ci.league.map(START)]
cv = read("step5_champion_vs_league.csv")
cv = cv[cv.season >= cv.league.map(START)]
ing = read("step5_champions_by_era.csv")
fcv = read("step5_final_title_cv.csv")
fsr = read("step5_final_series_cv.csv")
fsig = read("step5_final_significance.csv")
fw = read("step5_final_weights.csv")
prof = read("step5_league_profiles.csv")
yb = read("step5_wnba_years_behind.csv")
ERAS = {"NBA": ([2005, 2010, 2016, 2021, 2026], ["2006-10", "2011-16", "2017-21", "2022-26"]),
        "WNBA": ([2008, 2013, 2017, 2021, 2026], ["2009-13", "2014-17", "2018-21", "2022-26"])}
rng = np.random.default_rng(4)


def zone_summary(lg):
    rows = []
    for zone in ZONES:
        x = z[(z.league == lg) & (z.zone == zone)].pps_change.dropna().to_numpy()
        boots = [rng.choice(x, len(x)).mean() for _ in range(2000)]
        rows.append({"zone": zone, "seasons": len(x), "avg": x.mean(), "lo": np.percentile(boots, 2.5),
                     "hi": np.percentile(boots, 97.5), "worse": (x < 0).mean()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def zone_chart(lg):
    s = zone_summary(lg)
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_bar(y=s.zone, x=s.avg, orientation="h", marker=dict(color=LEAGUE[lg], line=dict(width=2, color="#fcfcfb")),
                error_x=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=s.hi - s.avg, arrayminus=s.avg - s.lo, color="#52514e", thickness=1.5),
                customdata=np.c_[s.lo, s.hi, s.worse],
                hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:+.3f} pts/shot<br>95%: %{customdata[0]:+.3f} to %{customdata[1]:+.3f}<br>worse in %{customdata[2]:.0%} of seasons<extra></extra>")
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.update_layout(height=280, hovermode="closest", xaxis_title="points per shot, playoffs minus regular season",
                      yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"), margin=dict(l=10, r=20, t=20, b=10))
    return fig, s


def zone_text(lg, s):
    s = s.set_index("zone")
    sure = [zn for zn in ZONES if s.loc[zn, "hi"] < 0]
    if not sure:
        return (f"**What this shows:** no {lg} shot zone has a reliable playoff change; every interval crosses zero. "
                "With few playoff teams each year the {lg} sample is small, so the honest reading is 'no clear penalty yet'.")
    worst = s.loc[sure].avg.idxmin()
    return (f"**What this shows:** bars left of zero are shots that get worse in the playoffs; the whiskers are 95% intervals. "
            f"In the {lg}, {', '.join(sure)} reliably lose value, with **{worst}** losing the most "
            f"({s.loc[worst, 'avg']:+.3f} points per shot, worse in {s.loc[worst, 'worse']:.0%} of seasons). "
            "Shots that cross zero hold up about as well as in the regular season.")


def identity_chart(lg):
    d = ci[ci.league == lg]
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.off_edge, y=d.def_edge, mode="markers", showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=10, color=LEAGUE[lg], line=dict(width=2, color="#fcfcfb")),
                    customdata=d[["season", "team", "off_rank", "def_rank", "n_teams", "identity"]],
                    hovertemplate="%{customdata[0]} %{customdata[1]}<br>offense #%{customdata[2]:.0f}, defense #%{customdata[3]:.0f} of %{customdata[4]}<br>%{customdata[5]}<extra></extra>")
    for _, row in d[d.season >= 2022].iterrows():
        fig.add_annotation(x=row.off_edge, y=row.def_edge, text=f"{row.team} {row.season % 100:02d}", showarrow=False,
                           yshift=13, font=dict(size=11))
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.update_layout(height=400, hovermode="closest", xaxis_title="offense edge vs league (pts/100)",
                      yaxis_title="defense edge vs league (pts/100)")
    return fig


def identity_text(lg):
    d = ci[ci.league == lg]
    n = d.identity.value_counts()
    rec = d[d.season >= 2022].sort_values("season")
    recent = "; ".join(f"{r.team} {r.season}: {r.identity}" for r in rec.itertuples())
    return (f"**What this shows:** each dot is a {lg} champion. Right = better offense than the league that season, "
            f"up = better defense. A champion is *offense-led* when its offensive edge beats its defensive edge by 3+ points per "
            f"100 possessions, *defense-led* the reverse, otherwise *balanced*. Of {len(d)} {lg} champions, "
            f"{n.get('balanced', 0)} were balanced, {n.get('offense-led', 0)} offense-led and {n.get('defense-led', 0)} defense-led "
            f"(these are counts of teams). Recent champions: {recent}.")


def champ_tables(lg):
    c = cv[cv.league == lg].copy()
    c["era"] = pd.cut(c.season, *ERAS[lg][:1], labels=ERAS[lg][1])
    cols = {"three_share_vs_league": "threes", "rim_share_vs_league": "rim", "mid_share_vs_league": "mid-range",
            "assisted_share_vs_league": "assisted makes"}
    g = c.groupby("era", observed=True)
    t = (g[list(cols)].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=cols)
    t.insert(0, "champions", g.size())
    i = ci[ci.league == lg].copy()
    i["era"] = pd.cut(i.season, *ERAS[lg][:1], labels=ERAS[lg][1])
    arch = [x for x in i.columns if x.startswith("arch_vs_league::")]
    a = (i.groupby("era", observed=True)[arch].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=lambda x: x.split("::")[1])
    return t.reset_index(), a.reset_index()


pos = read("champion_position_share.csv")
pos = pos[pos.season >= pos.league.map(START)]
POSN = {"G": "guards", "F": "forwards", "C": "centers"}


def position_table(lg):
    d = pos[pos.league == lg].copy()
    d["era"] = pd.cut(d.season, *ERAS[lg][:1], labels=ERAS[lg][1])
    g = d.groupby("era", observed=True)
    t = (g[["G_vs_league", "F_vs_league", "C_vs_league"]].mean() * 100).round(1)
    t.columns = ["guards", "forwards", "centers"]
    t.insert(0, "champions", g.size())
    return t.reset_index()


def composition_text(lg, arch):
    a = arch.set_index("era")
    p = position_table(lg).set_index("era")
    lines = []
    for era in a.index:
        row = a.loc[era]
        up, down = row.idxmax(), row.idxmin()
        pr = p.loc[era, ["guards", "forwards", "centers"]]
        pu = pr.idxmax()
        lines.append(f"- **{era}** ({int(p.loc[era, 'champions'])} champions): most extra minutes to **{up}** "
                     f"({row[up]:+.1f} points vs the league), fewest to **{down}** ({row[down]:+.1f}); by listed position, "
                     f"{pu} got the most extra minutes ({pr[pu]:+.1f}).")
    return "\n".join(lines)


HOW_TO_READ = (
    "**How to read these tables:** every number is the champions' average minus the league average that season, in "
    "percentage points of team minutes or shots. +5 means the champions gave 5 points more of their minutes (or shots) to "
    "that role than the average team did; 0 means they looked like everyone else. *Champions* is the number of title "
    "teams in that era. Positions are the listed G / F / C; archetypes describe how players actually play, so a team can "
    "have few centers but many interior roles, or the reverse.")


def title_section(lg):
    t = fcv[fcv.league == lg][["model", "mean_prob_on_champion", "champion_in_top3"]].copy()
    s = fsr[fsr.league == lg][["model", "accuracy"]]
    t = t.merge(s, on="model")
    t.columns = ["model", "avg chance given to the eventual champion", "champion in top 3", "playoff series called correctly"]
    for c in t.columns[1:]:
        t[c] = t[c].map(lambda x: f"{x:.0%}")
    w = fw[fw.league == lg].set_index("variable")
    g = fsig[(fsig.league == lg) & (fsig.model == "net rating + availability-adjusted strength")].iloc[0]
    txt = (f"**What this shows:** *net rating* is the team's points scored minus allowed per 100 possessions. "
           f"*Availability-adjusted strength* is our variable: the team rebuilt from this season's lineup-based player impact, "
           f"counting only the players available for the playoffs. Combined, our variable carries "
           f"**{w.loc['avail_now', 'share_of_total_weight']:.0%} of the model's weight** against "
           f"{w.loc['net', 'share_of_total_weight']:.0%} for net rating. Over every {lg} playoff series, adding it to net rating "
           f"improves predictions ({g.loglik_gain_per_series:+.3f} log-likelihood per series, one-sided p = {g.p_gain_le_0:.2f}).")
    return t.to_markdown(index=False), txt
```

```{python}
#| label: takeaways
nz = zone_summary("NBA").set_index("zone")
wz = zone_summary("WNBA")
m = yb[yb.wnba_season == yb.wnba_season.max()].set_index("feature")
c = cv[cv.season >= 2022].groupby("league")[["three_share_vs_league", "rim_share_vs_league"]].mean() * 100
nf = fsr[fsr.league == "NBA"].set_index("model").accuracy
md(f"""::: {{.callout-note appearance="simple"}}
## Takeaways
- **NBA playoffs punish threes and rim attempts.** Points per three fell in the playoffs in {nz.loc['three', 'worse']:.0%} of
  NBA seasons since 2005-06 ({nz.loc['three', 'avg']:+.3f} per shot); rim attempts in {nz.loc['rim', 'worse']:.0%}. Mid-range shots held up best.
- **WNBA playoffs:** {'no shot zone shows a reliable playoff change' if (wz.hi >= 0).all() else 'some zones lose value'}; with 8-12 playoff teams a year the sample is small.
- **WNBA {int(yb.wnba_season.max())}'s shot mix most resembles the NBA in {int(m.loc['three_share', 'nba_equivalent_season']) - 1}-{str(int(m.loc['three_share', 'nba_equivalent_season']))[-2:]}** on three-point share, which points to which NBA champions to study (below).
- **Recent champions vs their own league (2022-26):** WNBA champions {c.loc['WNBA', 'three_share_vs_league']:+.1f} points of shots from three and
  {c.loc['WNBA', 'rim_share_vs_league']:+.1f} at the rim; NBA champions {c.loc['NBA', 'three_share_vs_league']:+.1f} and {c.loc['NBA', 'rim_share_vs_league']:+.1f}.
- **Net rating plus our availability-adjusted strength predicts NBA playoff series better than net rating alone**
  ({nf['net rating + availability-adjusted strength']:.0%} vs {nf['net rating only (reference)']:.0%} called correctly).
:::""")
```

# NBA (2005-06 to 2025-26)

## NBA: which shots survive the playoffs?

```{python}
fig, s = zone_chart("NBA")
show(fig)
md(zone_text("NBA", s))
```

## NBA: champion identity

```{python}
show(identity_chart("NBA"))
md(identity_text("NBA"))
shot, arch = champ_tables("NBA")
md("**How NBA champions' shots differed from the league** (percentage points; + = more of that shot than the league)\n\n" + shot.to_markdown(index=False))
md("**NBA champions' archetype minutes minus the league average** (percentage points)\n\n" + arch.to_markdown(index=False))
md(HOW_TO_READ)
md("**NBA champions' minutes by listed position, minus the league average** (percentage points)\n\n" + position_table("NBA").to_markdown(index=False))
md("**Team composition, era by era:**\n\n" + composition_text("NBA", arch))
```

## NBA: picking champions and series

Trained season by season on earlier seasons only, with recent seasons weighted more (the weighting is chosen from past
seasons, never the one being predicted).

```{python}
t, txt = title_section("NBA")
md(t)
md(txt)
```

## WNBA: picking champions and series

The WNBA has 12-15 teams, so a random pick already has a 7-12% chance; every number here comes from 10 or fewer test seasons.

```{python}
t, txt = title_section("WNBA")
md(t)
md(txt)
```

# NBA vs WNBA: which NBA season does each WNBA season resemble?

This is not a measure of one league being "behind" the other. For each WNBA season, it finds the NBA season whose
shot mix is the same, so we can look at what won in that NBA season and ask whether the same patterns show up in the WNBA.

```{python}
fig = go.Figure()
for f, nm, col in [("three_share", "matched on share of shots from three", "#2a78d6"),
                   ("mid_share", "matched on share of shots from mid-range", "#eb6834")]:
    d = yb[(yb.feature == f) & (yb.wnba_season >= 2013)]
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.wnba_season, y=d.nba_equivalent_season, name=nm, mode="lines+markers",
                    line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=8, color=col),
                    hovertemplate="WNBA %{x} looks like NBA %{y:.0f}<extra></extra>")
fig.update_layout(height=360, xaxis_title="WNBA season", yaxis_title="closest NBA season", legend=dict(y=1.14),
                  hovermode="closest")
show(fig)
```

```{python}
champ = ci.set_index(["league", "season"])
rows = []
for s in range(2019, int(yb.wnba_season.max()) + 1):
    e = yb[(yb.wnba_season == s) & (yb.feature == "three_share")].nba_equivalent_season
    if e.empty or e.isna().all():
        continue
    n = int(round(e.iloc[0]))
    nb = champ.loc[("NBA", n)] if ("NBA", n) in champ.index else None
    wb = champ.loc[("WNBA", s)] if ("WNBA", s) in champ.index else None
    rows.append({"WNBA season": s, "closest NBA season": f"{n - 1}-{str(n)[-2:]}",
                 "NBA champion then": f"{nb.team} ({nb.identity})" if nb is not None else "",
                 "WNBA champion": f"{wb.team} ({wb.identity})" if wb is not None else ""})
md(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False))
md("**What this shows:** both lines rise together: as the WNBA has taken more threes and fewer mid-range shots, the NBA "
   "season it resembles has moved forward too, and by 2026 it matches the NBA of about 2019-20 on threes. The table pairs "
   "each recent WNBA season with its closest NBA season and both champions. Where the identities line up (for example "
   "balanced champions in both), the NBA's later seasons are a reasonable guide to what the WNBA may reward next; where "
   "they differ, the WNBA is following its own path.")
```

## Shot mix, both leagues

```{python}
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
p = prof[prof.season >= 2009]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("Share of shots from three", "Share of shots from mid-range"),
                    horizontal_spacing=0.1)
for j, f in enumerate(["three_share", "mid_share"], 1):
    for lg, col in LEAGUE.items():
        d = p[p.league == lg]
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.season, y=d[f], name=lg, legendgroup=lg, showlegend=(j == 1), mode="lines+markers",
                        line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=6, color=col),
                        hovertemplate=f"{lg}: " + "%{y:.1%}<extra></extra>", row=1, col=j)
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".0%")
fig.update_layout(height=360, legend=dict(y=1.16))
show(fig)
md("**What this shows:** both leagues are moving the same direction (more threes, fewer mid-range shots), the NBA "
   "earlier and faster. The WNBA's mid-range share has fallen most since 2020.")
```

::: {.caveat}
Association, not causation. Each league is measured against itself; NBA and WNBA numbers are compared, never pooled.
:::
